abstract: Motivation: Protein structure representations are often learned by reconstructing coordinates, yet reconstruction quality does not necessarily track performance on biological prediction tasks. We therefore investigate whether joint-embedding prediction can capture information useful for biological prediction while retaining recoverable backbone geometry. Results: We introduce PS-JEPA, a self-supervised model that learns protein structure representations by predicting masked residue embeddings from visible backbone context. The encoder combines geometric graph encoding with bidirectional Mamba and is pretrained without a coordinate-reconstruction objective. On StructTokenBench, frozen PS-JEPA representations achieve a mean remote-homology macro F1 (x100) of 72.24, compared with 67.12 for GearNet-Edge, the strongest baseline for this category, while remaining competitive in functional and flexibility prediction. A separately trained decoder reconstructs backbones from these frozen representations, achieving a mean C RMSD of 1.61 [A] on 309 external test chains filtered to exclude sequence matches to training and reference data. In an exploratory test of unconditional generation, a learned latent prior with the same decoder yields 62 of 384 backbones (16.15%) that meet the computational designability criterion. Together, these results show that joint-embedding prediction can learn representations that support both biological prediction and backbone reconstruction. Availability and Implementation: https://github.com/ahexlwang/PS-JEPA
